title: Spinal Cord Anatomy: Gray Horns, White Tracts & Pathway
description: Master spinal cord anatomy in cross-section and length, from dorsal sensory and ventral motor roots to gray matter horns, white tracts, and spinal segment.
h1: Spinal Cord Anatomy: Gray Matter Horns, White Tracts and Roots
blurb: Protected inside the vertebral canal, a butterfly core of gray-matter neuron horns is surrounded by ascending sensory and descending motor white-matter tracts.
lead: Running through the protective tunnel of the vertebral column, the spinal cord is a two-way superhighway linking the brain with every trunk and limb segment. This illustrated study guide examines 22 documented anatomical entries—including Posterior (dorsal) horn, Anterior (ventral) horn, Lateral horn—connecting visible form, tissue organization, and physiological function.

Running through the protective tunnel of the vertebral column, the spinal cord is a two-way superhighway linking the brain with every trunk and limb segment. Known in classical anatomical nomenclature as Medulla spinalis, this chapter belongs to the nervous study pathway. In cross-section the cord shows an H- or butterfly-shaped core of grey matter — posterior (sensory) horns, lateral (autonomic) horns in thoracic segments and anterior (motor) horns — around the central canal. White matter surrounds it in funiculi carrying the dorsal column–medial lemniscus (fine touch, proprioception), the spinothalamic tracts (pain, temperature) and the corticospinal tracts (voluntary movement). Dorsal roots carry sensory fibres with their cell bodies in the dorsal root ganglion; ventral roots carry motor fibres. Three meninges and the denticulate ligaments suspend the cord in CSF.

When you trace how spinal cord anatomy functions in the living body, each documented landmark contributes a specific mechanical or physiological step. Key structures covered in this guide include Posterior (dorsal) horn (first synapse for pain, temperature and touch; gate control of nociception happens here), Anterior (ventral) horn (final common pathway: alpha motor neurons innervate skeletal muscle), Lateral horn (origin of the sympathetic outflow), and Central canal (circulates a trickle of CSF within the cord). By following all 22 illustrated landmarks in sequence, you can see how gross morphology, internal chambers or layers, and surrounding vessels work as one integrated unit.

Understanding these structural relationships is essential for both anatomy exams and real-world physiological reasoning. Practical anatomical correlations also stand out: for posterior (dorsal) horn, loss of the spinothalamic decussation at a segment causes a segmental band of lost pain and temperature (syringomyelia); for anterior (ventral) horn, poliovirus and ALS destroy these cells, giving flaccid paralysis, wasting and fasciculation. questions.question: Where does the spinal cord end in adults?
questions.answer: The spinal cord usually tapers to the conus medullaris near the L1-L2 vertebral level in adults; nerve roots continue below it as the cauda equina. From an anatomical and functional standpoint, compression may cause saddle sensory and sphincter symptoms.

questions.question: What is the difference between gray and white matter in the spinal cord?
questions.answer: Central gray matter contains neuronal cell bodies and local circuits; surrounding white matter carries ascending sensory and descending motor pathways. In relation to dorsal root & ganglion, this structure carries all afferent input from one dermatome.

questions.question: What is the posterior (dorsal) horn?
questions.answer: The slender upper horns receiving sensory afferents; laminae I–VI including the substantia gelatinosa. Function: First synapse for pain, temperature and touch; gate control of nociception happens here. In relation to posterior (dorsal) horn, this structure first synapse for pain, temperature and touch; gate control of nociception happens here.

questions.question: Where is the lateral horn located?
questions.answer: Present only in T1–L2, holding preganglionic sympathetic neurons (and S2–S4 parasympathetic equivalents). Function: Origin of the sympathetic outflow. In relation to lateral horn, this structure origin of the sympathetic outflow. From an anatomical and functional standpoint, horner syndrome follows interruption of the T1 lateral horn or its pathway (e.g. Pancoast tumour).

questions.question: What is the function of the white funiculi & tracts?
questions.answer: Function: Highways for sensation upward and motor commands downward. Dorsal columns (fasciculus gracilis & cuneatus), lateral spinothalamic and corticospinal tracts, and spinocerebellar tracts. In relation to white funiculi & tracts, this structure highways for sensation upward and motor commands downward.
